blocks.text: It remains for us to say briefly why, for the whole species, the Law forbids only the eating of the daughter of יענה jaana, that is, of the ostrich; this torments the Hebrews not a little. In Aben Ezra on this passage some answer, שהוא מין שלא ימצאו זכרים כמו הארנבת, that it is a species of animal which has no males, just as the hare has none. And they say it is objected in vain that in Thren. IV, 3. יענים jeenim has a masculine form, since יעלים jeelim, ibexes, and רחלים rechelim, ewes, are of the same form, and yet they are feminine. He himself, above on Exod. XXIII, 29., answered that in the whole species of ostriches only the daughter is forbidden, that is, only the females among the chicks, because that alone is edible: the mothers cannot be eaten, nor even the male chicks, and the adults much less. Rabbi Moses, son of Maimon, in the book On Forbidden Foods, right at the beginning of chapter 3, understands by the daughter of the ostrich its egg. Whatever, he says, is produced by a forbidden species of animal is itself also forbidden, for instance the milk of a beast of burden or of an unclean wild animal, וביצי עוף ודג הטמאים שנ׳ ואת בת היענה זו ביצתה והוא הדין לכל האסור כיענה ולכל הדברים הדומים לביצה, And the eggs of an unclean bird or fish, according to what is said (in the Law), „And the daughter of jaana“ (that is, of the ostrich, you shall not eat), that is, its egg: and the same Law applies to every animal that is forbidden like the ostrich, and to everything that is like an egg. [II, 827] So the Hebrews, but most absurdly. First, what some assert is utterly false, that either ostriches or hares or any other kind of animal has only females; it is also contrary to the express words of Scripture, Gen. VII, 2. 3. 19. Nor is Aben Ezra's view any truer, that only the female of the ostrich is edible, and that only before it is full-grown. For the geographers and historians, to whom so many occasions present themselves of treating this subject, would not have omitted it. Nor could the physicians have passed it over untouched without sin, when they write on the choice of foods and on the rank in which ostriches are to be held. To prove that Firmus was a great glutton, and above all swallowed a great deal of meat, Vopiscus reports that he ate an ostrich in a day. But from a man of huge stature, so that most people called him a Cyclops, and who, when challenged to drink, drained two buckets full of unmixed wine, from such a man, I say, it would be no marvel that an ostrich was eaten in one day, if a chick were meant, hatched from the egg not long before. Maimonides too trifles, contrary to his custom, when he wants the daughter of the ostrich to be understood as its egg. For that a chick should be called a son is tolerable, and this catachresis is accepted, since Columella, book 7, chapter 36, writes of the onager, A stallion of this kind is more useful for grandchildren than for children. And the proverb is commonplace in Juvenal and others,

— son of a white hen. But that an egg should be called the daughter of a hen was never heard of. And if the egg is called a son, the chick born from that egg will have to be called not the hen's son but her grandson. And in these words of the Prophets, There the daughters of the ostrich shall dwell. There shall be a pasture of the daughters of the ostrich. The daughters of the ostrich shall glorify me, says the Lord. I will make a mourning like the daughters of the ostrich; I was a companion of the daughters of the ostrich, etc., the daughters of the ostrich would be understood as eggs. As though eggs dwell, or feed, or make mourning, or have companions, etc.: which is utterly absurd. Finally, if בת יענה bath jaana is not the animal itself but only the egg, God would have forbidden the Jews only the eating of the egg, and not the animal itself. Which not even they themselves would [col. 230] concede.
